results.proposed_proof:
**Given:** The reduced monad and its pairing as stated.

[A1] AC is inherited through the analytic sheaf-cohomology supplier. [[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] The reduced splitting has $H^0(F_M)=0$, is trivial and positive on each real line, and retains a nondegenerate middle Hermitian form. [[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-flat-splitting]]

[F2] The analytic hyperplane calculation supplies $H^0(\mathbb P^1,\mathcal O(-1))=0$. [[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-analytic-twist-cohomology]]

[F3] The bundle and Hermitian conventions are locally trivial holomorphic bundles with first-slot-linear Hermitian pairings. [[def-complex-manifolds-and-holomorphic-vector-bundles]]



**Given:** Let $S=M$, and choose coordinates identifying the end space $U'$ with $U^*$ by the lifted pairing. All transposes below are complex-linear duals, while daggers are Hermitian adjoints.

1.1 Define $S_d=S\oplus S^*$ and $R=U\oplus U^*$. On $S_d$ put $$ \omega((s,\phi),(t,\psi))=\phi^Tt-\psi^Ts,\qquad J(s,\phi)=(H^{-1}\bar\phi,-H^T\bar s). $$ Then $\omega$ is a nondegenerate complex-bilinear alternating form, $J$ is antilinear, $J^2=-1$, and $\omega(Jx,Jy)=\overline{\omega(x,y)}$ by direct substitution and $H^\dagger=H$. Consequently $\omega(Jx,y)=-\overline{\omega(x,Jy)}$ and $h_d(Jx,Jy)=h_d(y,x)$. Thus $h_d(x,y)=\omega(x,Jy)$ is a nondegenerate first-slot-linear Hermitian form with matrix $\operatorname{diag}(H,H^{-T})$. [A1, F3, algebra]

1.2 Fix $z\ne0$ and write $A_z=\alpha(z)$, $B_z=\alpha(jz)$. On the real line spanned by $z,jz$, its linear coordinate $(a,b)$ gives $\alpha(a,b)=aA_z+bB_z$ and $\beta(a,b)=aB_z^\dagger H-bA_z^\dagger H$. Expanding $\beta(a,b)\alpha(a,b)=0$ in $a,b$ gives $A_z^\dagger HB_z=B_z^\dagger HA_z=0$ and $A_z^\dagger HA_z=B_z^\dagger HB_z=:G_z$. The matrix $G_z$ is invertible: if $G_zv=0$ for $v\ne0$, injectivity of $A_z$ gives $A_zv\ne0$, while $\beta(a,b)A_zv=0$ for every $(a,b)$. Its class is a global section of the trivial bundle $F_M|_\ell$ vanishing at $(1,0)$, hence is identically zero; exactness on $\ell$ would then put the constant $A_zv$ in the image of $H^0(U\otimes\mathcal O_\ell(-1))=0$, a contradiction by [F2]. [F1, F2, algebra]

2.1 Define $a_d(z)=\operatorname{diag}(\alpha(z),\beta(z)^T):R\to S_d$ and the complex-linear map $\Phi:R\otimes\mathbb C^4\to S_d$ by $\Phi(r\otimes z)=a_d(z)r$. Let $c(u,\phi)=(\bar\phi,\bar u)$, the antilinear involution of $R$. The two identities for $\beta$ give $J a_d(z)=a_d(jz)c$. Also $\operatorname{im}a_d(z)$ is $\omega$-isotropic, since its pairing is the transpose of $\beta(z)\alpha(z)=0$. Consequently $\mathscr H=\Phi^*h_d$ satisfies $\mathscr H((c\otimes j)x,(c\otimes j)y)=\mathscr H(y,x)$ and $R\otimes z\perp_{\mathscr H}R\otimes jz$. [given, step 1.1, algebra]

2.2 The two images $\operatorname{im}A_z$ and $\operatorname{im}B_z$ are therefore nondegenerate and $H$-orthogonal. Their orthogonal complement $$ E_z=\ker(A_z^\dagger H)\cap\ker(B_z^\dagger H) $$ is the section space of $F_M|_\ell$: in bases given by $A_z,B_z$ and $G_z^{-1}$, the first two summands form copies of the exact Euler complex $\mathcal O(-1)\to\mathcal O^2\to\mathcal O(1)$, and the remaining summand is $E_z\otimes\mathcal O$. Thus $H|_{E_z}$ is positive by [F1]. The doubled target complement is $E_z\oplus E_z^*$, on which $h_d$ is positive. [F1, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 The form $\mathscr H$ is nondegenerate on $R\otimes z$ because its Gram matrix there is $\operatorname{diag}(G_z,G_z^T)$. Its orthogonal complement to $(R\otimes z)\oplus(R\otimes jz)$ maps by $\Phi$ into $E_z\oplus E_z^*$; hence $\mathscr H$ is nonnegative on that complement, with $\ker\Phi$ allowed. Moreover $\Phi$ is onto: the images of the $\alpha_i$ span $M$ by definition, and the annihilator of the span of the $\beta_i^T$ is $\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i=H^0(F_M)=0$ by [F1]. This verifies the linewise orthogonality, nondegeneracy, and complement-positivity hypotheses needed for the following finite matrix calculation. [F1, step 2.1, step 2.2, algebra]

3.2 Use the original middle space $S=M$ and its constant Hermitian matrix $H$, rather than the doubled coefficient space, for the remaining positivity calculation. Put $z_1=x_1+ix_2$, $z_2=x_3+ix_4$ and $$ a(x)=\alpha(1,0,z_1,z_2)=a_0+z_1M_1+z_2M_2,\qquad b(x)=\alpha(0,1,-\bar z_2,\bar z_1)=b_0-\bar z_2M_1+\bar z_1M_2. $$ The two arguments are $z,jz$ in the stated coordinate convention. Step 1.2 gives $$ a^\dagger Ha=b^\dagger Hb=A(x),\qquad a^\dagger Hb=0, $$ with $A(x)$ invertible for every $x$. Apply the same identities on the infinity line with $z=(0,0,1,0)$ and $jz=(0,0,0,1)$ to obtain $$ M_1^\dagger HM_1=M_2^\dagger HM_2=C,\qquad M_1^\dagger HM_2=0, $$ where $C$ is invertible. Neither $A(x)$ nor $C$ is yet assumed positive. Let $K=A^{-1}$ and $$ Q=1-aKa^\dagger H-bKb^\dagger H. $$ The Gram identities imply $Q^2=Q$ and $Q^\dagger H=HQ$; its range is precisely the real-line section complement $E_z$ in step 2.2. Thus $y^\dagger HQy=(Qy)^\dagger H(Qy)\ge0$ for every $y$, by the actual induced section pairing there. This identification uses the lifted identity $\beta=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and the Euler-complex decomposition of step 2.2; it is not an extra assumption of positivity of $H$ on the coefficient images. [given, F1, step 1.2, step 2.2, algebra]

4.1 Put $P=a^\dagger HM_1$ and $R=a^\dagger HM_2$. Differentiating $a^\dagger Hb=0$ in $x_1,x_3$ gives $a^\dagger HM_2=-M_1^\dagger Hb$ and $a^\dagger HM_1=M_2^\dagger Hb$, hence $b^\dagger HM_1=-R^\dagger$ and $b^\dagger HM_2=P^\dagger$. Since $a_\mu=(M_1,iM_1,M_2,iM_2)$, the derivatives of $A$ are $$ A_1=P+P^\dagger,\quad A_2=iP-iP^\dagger,\quad A_3=R+R^\dagger,\quad A_4=iR-iR^\dagger. $$ Pairing the real and imaginary derivatives, with the matrix order retained, gives $$ \sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu =2(PKP^\dagger+P^\dagger KP+RKR^\dagger+R^\dagger KR) =\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger H(1-Q)a_\mu. $$ The second equality follows by substituting $1-Q=aKa^\dagger H+bKb^\dagger H$ and the displayed formulas for $b^\dagger HM_i$. As $\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger Ha_\mu=4C$, set $$ D=\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger HQa_\mu =\sum_\mu(Qa_\mu)^\dagger H(Qa_\mu)\succeq0; \qquad \sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu=4C-D. $$ Also $\Delta A=2\sum_\mu a_\mu^\dagger Ha_\mu=8C$. Differentiating $AK=1$ twice therefore yields $$ \Delta K=2K\Big(\sum_\mu A_\mu K A_\mu\Big)K-K(\Delta A)K =-2KDK\preceq0. $$ This last inequality is congruence by the Hermitian matrix $K$, and does not assume its positivity. Thus for every constant $v\in U$, $f_v(x)=v^\dagger K(x)v$ is a real smooth function with $\Delta f_v\le0$ on all of $\mathbb R^4$. [step 3.2, algebra]

5.1 Expanding the Gram gives $A(x)=|x|^2C+O(|x|)$ uniformly in direction. Since $C$ is invertible, writing $A=r^2(C+E_r)$ with $\|E_r\|=O(r^{-1})$ and using the convergent geometric series for $(1+C^{-1}E_r)^{-1}$ proves $\|K(x)\|\le2\|C^{-1}\|r^{-2}$ for all sufficiently large $r$. In particular $f_v$ tends uniformly to zero at infinity. On a closed ball of radius $R$, the function $f_v-\delta|x|^2$ has strictly negative Laplacian for $\delta>0$ and cannot attain a minimum in the interior, where its real Hessian would be positive semidefinite. Hence $f_v(x)\ge\min_{|y|=R}f_v(y)-\delta R^2$. First let $\delta\downarrow0$, then let $R\to\infty$ with $x$ fixed. The uniform decay proves $f_v(x)\ge0$. Thus $K$ is positive semidefinite; being Hermitian and invertible, it is positive definite, as is $A$. At any fixed $x$, the $H$-orthogonal direct decomposition $$ S=\operatorname{im}a\oplus\operatorname{im}b\oplus\operatorname{range}Q $$ has positive Gram $A$ on its first two summands and the positive section form of step 2.2 on the third. Therefore $H$ is positive definite. If $U=0$, $Q=1$ and the section positivity already gives this conclusion directly; no inverse of a nonzero-dimensional Gram is needed. The preceding splitting lemma retains the positive constant flat summand separately. This proves the stated arbitrary-rank claim without a coefficient-span surjectivity assumption or a transpose Clifford identity. [F1, step 2.2, step 3.2, step 4.1, algebra] ∎

**Given:** The monad, its real-line trivializations, positive pairing and
unitary infinity framing from the Statement, together with its explicit
first-order extension when the family clause is used.

[A1] Under full AC, the batch-67 scalar cohomology theorem states
$H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$ and
$H^q(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ for $q>0$ for $0\le r\le3$.
[[thm-qftx-gaga-analytic-projective-dolbeault-scalar-cohomology]]

[A2] Full AC is the stated axiom base inherited by the analytic and
finite-dimensional suppliers used in this construction.
[[def-axiom-of-choice]]

[F1] Under the negative-twist vanishings derived from [A1], every holomorphic
map of the stated monad cohomology bundles lifts uniquely to a constant chain
map; the signed self-dual lift is Hermitian and obeys
$\beta(z)=\alpha(jz)^\dagger H$ and
$\beta(jz)^\dagger=-H\alpha(z)$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-chain-lift]]

[F9] The analytic negative-twist groups $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-1))=0$
for all $q$ and $H^q(\mathbb P^3,\mathcal O(-2))=0$ for $q=0,1,2$ follow from
the hyperplane sequences and the scalar cohomology input.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-analytic-twist-cohomology]]

[F2] The constant global section space is
$L=\bigcap_i\ker\beta_i=M^{\perp_H}$ for
$M=\sum_i\operatorname{im}\alpha_i$; the monad splits orthogonally as
$L\otimes\mathcal O$ plus a reduced monad with no global sections, and the
form on $L$ and every real-line section space is positive.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-flat-splitting]]

[F3] On the reduced monad, the lifted middle Hermitian form is positive
definite; the proof identifies the actual real-line positive complement and
uses its inverse-Gram Laplacian inequality, uniform decay and the elementary
minimum principle, without assuming a sign for the infinity Gram matrix.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-internal-positivity]]

[F4] The ADHM convention is
$\mu_{\mathbb C}=[B_1,B_2]+IJ$,
$\mu_{\mathbb R}=[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J$;
stability is the word-span condition and costability is the invariant-kernel
condition.
[[def-qftx-adhm-linear-data-stability-and-regularity]]

[F5] For these raw coefficients, affine injectivity of $a_z$ is equivalent to
costability, affine surjectivity of $b_z^\dagger$ is equivalent to stability,
and zero moments plus regularity give the displayed homogeneous bundle monad.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-rank-stability-criterion]]

[F6] A first-order family is a locally split monad of free modules over
$A=\mathbb C[\epsilon]/(\epsilon^2)$ with locally free cohomology commuting
with reduction, free global sections and a direct-summand coefficient image
commuting with reduction, and trivial real-line restrictions whose section
modules commute with reduction; positivity is imposed on its reduced section
forms, and the allowed base maps are reduction and
$\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ for real $r$.
[[def-qftx-positive-real-monad-first-order-families]]

[F7] The finite algebraic resolution gives
$\operatorname{ch}(F)=N-kH^2$, $c_1(F)=0$, $c_2(F)=kH^2$,
$\chi(F)=N-2k$; its line cycle class is the topological hyperplane class, and
the positive incidence fiber calculation gives $\pi^*u=H^2$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-charge-normalization]]

[F8] At zero real moment level, regular complex orbits correspond to unique
unitary orbits. This applies to the extracted stable data and is used only
when passing from the explicit framed chain classification to the usual
zero-level ADHM quotient.
[[thm-qftx-adhm-real-complex-quotient-correspondence]]

[F10] For each integer $m$, the analytic hyperplane sequence is
$0\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m-1)\to\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^r}(m)\to i_*\mathcal O_{\mathbb P^{r-1}}(m)\to0$.
[[lem-qftx-positive-real-monad-hyperplane-twist-sequences]]

[F11] For any commutative coefficient ring $A$, the algebraic twisting-sheaf theorem gives $H^0(\mathbb P^3_A,\mathcal O)=A$, acyclicity of $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$, and homogeneous-polynomial global sections in nonnegative degree. In its Laurent-monomial calculation the modules and maps commute with coefficient homomorphisms. This is used for the algebraic $\operatorname{Proj}A$ family objects, not as an analytic GAGA assertion.
[[thm-cohomology-projective-space-twisting-sheaves]]



**Given:** The Statement's monad and pairing, and [A1] whenever analytic
cohomology is used.

1.1 First the holomorphic monad maps have homogeneous linear entries. Indeed, in the $m=1$ sequence of [F10], $H^1(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O)=0$ by [A1], so restriction $H^0(\mathbb P^r,\mathcal O(1))\to H^0(\mathbb P^{r-1},\mathcal O(1))$ is surjective and its kernel is the defining hyperplane coordinate times $H^0(\mathcal O)=\mathbb C$. Starting with $r=0$, where $\mathcal O(1)$ on a point has one-dimensional section space, induction shows that every section is a linear combination of the homogeneous coordinates: subtract the global coordinate lifts of its restriction, then the remaining section is a constant multiple of the defining coordinate. This applies to entries of both $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O(-1),\mathcal O)$ and $\operatorname{Hom}(\mathcal O,\mathcal O(1))$. Thus no algebraic/analytic comparison is needed to introduce their four coefficient maps. By [A1] and [F9], the hyperplane sequences and analytic scalar theorem give exactly the negative-twist vanishings required by [F1]. Apply [F1] to the pairing isomorphism; it gives the unique constant Hermitian lift $H$ with the signed identities there. Thus no algebraic cohomology group is being substituted for the analytic lifting groups. [A1, A2, F1, F9, F10, construct]

1.2 For the algebraic $\mathbb P^3_A=\operatorname{Proj}A[\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\mu_1,\mu_2]$ family category, [F11] directly supplies the needed $\mathcal O(-1)$ and $\mathcal O(-2)$ groups over $A$ and $H^0(\mathcal O_A)=A$. Separately, on the analytic first-order thickening each twist has the split underlying analytic sheaf $\mathcal O_A(d)=\mathcal O(d)\oplus\epsilon\mathcal O(d)$; finite direct sums commute with sheaf cohomology, so [F9] gives the same vanishings there. Thus a holomorphic family pairing can be lifted analytically, whereas algebraic family sheaves use [F11]; neither computation substitutes algebraic cohomology for an analytic group or invokes GAGA. Both yield constant $A$-valued chain maps. In both categories the two kernel/image sequences identify global sections with the same constant coefficient kernel of $\beta_A$, so the specified global-section base-change condition is respected by this identification. Repeating the obstruction and ambiguity calculation of [F1] over these coefficient modules lifts the family pairing uniquely to an $A$-linear constant chain isomorphism with Hermitian middle matrix $H_A$; its inverse exists because its reduction is invertible. Global section base change identifies $H^0(F_A)$ with the constant coefficient kernel $L_A$ in $S_A$. Its reduction is injective, so a full-rank minor is a unit and $L_A$ is a direct summand. [A1, A2, F1, F6, F9, F11, construct]

2.1 By [F2], the global constant subspace $L$ is positive and $S=L\oplus M$ orthogonally, and the reduced monad on $M$ preserves the full framing. Apply [F3] to that reduced monad; it proves $H|_M$ positive. Since $H|_L$ is positive and the sum is orthogonal, $H$ is positive definite on all of $S$. In particular the argument also covers $k=0$, where $M=0$. [F2, F3, step 1.1]

2.2 By hypothesis the coefficient-image module $M_A$ is a direct summand. The coefficient identities give $M_A^\perp=L_A$; for a direct summand in a finite free module with a perfect pairing, the restriction map to its dual is split-surjective, so taking orthogonal complements twice returns that summand. Hence $M_A=L_A^\perp$ and $S_A=L_A\oplus M_A$. The line-section base change and the vanishing $H^0(\ell_A,\mathcal O(-1))=0$ make restriction of $L_A$ injective; the reduced line positivity makes $H_A|_{L_0}$ positive. The internal-positivity proof applies to the reduction on $M_0$, so its reduced form is positive too. On infinity the family framing identifies the remaining orthogonal complement isometrically with $W_A$. [F1, F2, F3, F6, F9, step 1.2, algebra]

3.1 Write the four coefficient maps of $\alpha$ as $P=\alpha_{\lambda_1}$, $Q=\alpha_{\lambda_2}$, $R=\alpha_{\mu_1}$, and $T=\alpha_{\mu_2}$. From the first-slot convention and $j^2=-1$, the corresponding coefficients of $\beta$ are $Q^\dagger H,-P^\dagger H,T^\dagger H,-R^\dagger H$ in that order. The $\mu_1^2,\mu_2^2,\mu_1\mu_2$ coefficients of $\beta\alpha=0$ give $T^\dagger HR=R^\dagger HT=0$ and $R^\dagger HR=T^\dagger HT$. The maps $R,T$ are injective by exactness at the two coordinate points of $\ell_\infty$. Positivity of $H$ therefore makes their common Gram matrix $G$ positive definite. Replacing the paired end bases by $G^{-1/2}$ normalizes both maps to isometries with orthogonal images. Choosing an orthonormal basis of $S$ then identifies $R=-\iota_1$, $T=-\iota_2$ and $S=(V\oplus V)\oplus W_0$, with $W_0$ their orthogonal complement. [given, step 2.1, algebra]

4.1 At infinity the maps are $\alpha_\infty=-\mu_1\iota_1-\mu_2\iota_2$ and $\beta_\infty=\mu_2\iota_1^\dagger-\mu_1\iota_2^\dagger$. For every $[\mu_1:\mu_2]\in\mathbb P^1$, the kernel of $\beta_\infty$ in $V\oplus V$ is the line-valued copy $\{(\mu_1v,\mu_2v):v\in V\}$, which is exactly the image of $\alpha_\infty$; $W_0$ is killed by $\beta_\infty$ and meets that image trivially. Therefore the restricted cohomology and its section pairing are canonically $W_0\otimes\mathcal O_{\ell_\infty}$ and its standard positive form. The specified unitary framing identifies $W_0$ with $W$ without discarding any flat summand. [step 3.1, given, algebra]

4.2 Relative to $S=V\oplus V\oplus W$, write $P=(B_1,B_2,J)^T$ and $Q=(Q_1,Q_2,Q_W)^T$. The coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_1$ in $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HR+T^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_1=-B_2^\dagger$; the coefficient of $\lambda_1\mu_2$ is $Q^\dagger HT-R^\dagger HP=0$, so $Q_2=B_1^\dagger$. Define $I^\dagger=Q_W$. These definitions give exactly the displayed $\alpha$ and, by the lifted reality identity, the displayed $\beta$. [step 3.1, algebra]

5.1 The $\lambda_1^2$ coefficient of $\beta\alpha=0$ is $Q^\dagger HP=0$. Substitution of the blocks gives $-[B_2,B_1]+IJ=[B_1,B_2]+IJ=0$. The $\lambda_1\lambda_2$ coefficient is $Q^\dagger HQ-P^\dagger HP=0$. Expanding it gives $[B_1,B_1^\dagger]+[B_2,B_2^\dagger]+II^\dagger-J^\dagger J=0$, which is $\mu_{\mathbb R}=0$. Conversely, these two moment equations make all coefficients of $\beta\alpha$ vanish, and direct substitution yields $$ \beta\alpha=\lambda_1^2\mu_{\mathbb C} +\lambda_1\lambda_2\mu_{\mathbb R} -\lambda_2^2\mu_{\mathbb C}^\dagger=0. $$ [step 4.2, algebra]

5.2 Let a normalized framed chain isomorphism have domain, middle and target maps $g_-,g_0,g_+$. It preserves $H$, so $g_0$ is unitary. Comparing the two $\mu$ coefficients forces $g_0|_{V\oplus0}=g_-$ and $g_0|_{0\oplus V}=g_-$; unitarity then preserves $W_0$. The infinity framing is fixed, so $g_0|_{W_0}=1$. Thus $g_0=\operatorname{diag}(g,g,1)$ for one $g\in U(V)$, and the $\lambda$ coefficients force $B_i'=gB_ig^{-1}$, $I'=gI$, and $J'=Jg^{-1}$. Surjectivity of $\beta$ makes $g_+$ uniquely determined and equal to $g$. Conversely, each such $g$ defines the displayed pairing-preserving framed chain isomorphism. Hence there are no residual transformations beyond simultaneous $U(V)$. [step 3.1, step 4.1, step 4.2, algebra]

6.1 On the affine chart $[\lambda_1:\lambda_2:\mu_1:\mu_2] =[1:0:z_1:z_2]$, the raw maps are $a_z$ and $b_z^\dagger$ from [F5]. Since the original $\alpha,\beta$ have their required ranks at every point, [F5] gives costability and stability. Thus the extracted zero-moment datum is regular. Conversely, for stable and costable data, [F5] proves full homogeneous rank, composition zero, and local splitting, so the raw formula does define the required monad. [F4, F5, step 5.1, algebra]

6.2 Put $B_1'=t_1B_1$, $B_2'=t_2B_2$, $I'=Ih^{-1}$, and $J'=t_1t_2hJ$. Substituting $(\lambda_1,t_1t_2\lambda_2,t_1\mu_1,t_2\mu_2)$ into the primed $A,C$ gives $A'=t_1A$ and $C'=t_2C$. Substitution into $\alpha'$ then gives $$ \alpha'(g_tz)(t_1t_2)^{-1} =\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)\alpha(z). $$ The same substitution into $\beta'$ gives $\beta'(g_tz)\operatorname{diag}(t_2^{-1},t_1^{-1},h)=\beta(z)$. The factors therefore are the stated chain maps; on the framed flavor coordinates $h=\operatorname{diag}(e_a^{-1})$ supplies the stated weights. [step 4.2, step 5.1, algebra]

6.3 After lifting reduced orthonormal bases, the common Gram matrix of the two $\mu$ coefficient maps has the form $I+\epsilon K$ with $K=K^\dagger$. The change $T=I-\tfrac12\epsilon K$ satisfies $T^\dagger(I+\epsilon K)T=I$ using $\epsilon^2=0$ and $\bar\epsilon=\epsilon$. This normalizes both $\mu$ maps over $A$ without ordering nilpotent elements or asserting nilpotent positivity. Choices of lifted normalized bases differ by the residual $U(k,A)$ action proved in step 5.2, so coefficient extraction is independent of those choices on isomorphism classes. [F6, step 3.1, step 5.2, step 2.2, algebra]

7.1 For any such raw datum and finite $z$, write $a_z=(B_1-z_1,B_2-z_2,J)^T$ and $b_z^\dagger=(-B_2+z_2,B_1-z_1,I)$. The two moment equations give $b_z^\dagger a_z=0$ and $a_z^\dagger a_z=b_z^\dagger b_z=:f_z$. Regularity makes both maps full rank, so $f_z$ is positive definite. On $\ell_z$ the monad is $\alpha=a_z\lambda_1+b_z\lambda_2$ and $\beta=b_z^\dagger\lambda_1-a_z^\dagger\lambda_2$. The cross Gram terms vanish, and $a_z,b_z$ identify two orthogonal copies of $V$ after applying $f_z^{-1/2}$. In these orthonormal coordinates the end maps on the first two copies are $(\lambda_1,\lambda_2)^T$ and $(-\lambda_2,\lambda_1)$, the Euler complex $V\mathcal O(-1)\to(V\oplus V)\mathcal O\to V\mathcal O(1)$; the complementary term is $E_z\mathcal O$. Hence $H^0(F|_{\ell_z})=E_z$ with its positive induced form, and $F|_{\ell_z}$ is trivial. At infinity the same calculation in step 4.1 gives $W\otimes\mathcal O$ and its framing. The maps in step 6.1 are exactly the required locally split end maps. [F5, step 4.1, step 5.1, step 6.1, algebra]

7.2 The zero-level quotient result [F8] applies because step 6.1 established stability and both zero moments; it identifies each stable complex orbit with its unique unitary orbit. The explicit argument in step 5.2 is stronger for the framed real monads: it identifies their actual normalized isomorphisms with $U(V)$ and fixes the inverse extraction orbit. If a constant flat summand is present, [F2] places it in the framed $W_0$ complement and the same fixed-frame argument leaves it unchanged. When $k=0$, every map into or out of $V=0$ is zero and $U(0)$ has one element. Because all coefficient images lie in $M=L^\perp$, $J$ has no component in the framed flat subspace $L\subset W$ and $I$ vanishes on that subspace. Thus flat directions remain as unused directions of $W$. [F2, F4, F8, step 6.1, step 5.2, algebra]

7.3 The coefficient equations in steps 4.2–3.2 are polynomial identities, so over $A$ they give the same block form and both moment equations. Conversely, take an $A$-valued zero-moment datum whose reduction is regular. Every full-rank minor of its reduced raw maps lifts to a unit in the local rings of the first-order thickening; thus the end maps are locally split and the cohomology is locally free. On a fixed real line the matrices $a_z,b_z$ have full-rank reductions, so their common Gram $f_z$ is invertible over $A$. Their orthogonal images split off two free copies of $V_A$, leaving a free rank-$N$ complement; the line complex is the Euler complex plus that constant complement, so its sections commute with reduction. The global section and coefficient-image conditions are exactly the additional range conditions imposed in the Statement. The standard middle form induces a nondegenerate real pairing, positive after reduction. Thus such data give families in the stated range. The proof of step 5.2 uses only coefficient comparison, the framing, and $g^\dagger g=1$, so it gives exactly $U(k,A)$ as the residual group. Reduction and each map $\epsilon\mapsto r\epsilon$ commute with coefficient extraction and with the correction $T$. This proves first-order naturality for precisely the stated base changes. [F6, step 4.2, step 5.1, step 5.2, step 6.3, algebra]

8.1 The finite monad resolution and its locally free cohomology give the algebraic Chern character and Chern classes in [F7]. Its same finite line resolution yields the topological classes after the hyperplane cycle class is identified with the Euler class of the complex normal line. The positive incidence-fiber Thom calculation in [F7] gives $\pi^*u=H_{\rm top}^2$. If the topological bundle is $\pi^*E$, naturality gives $\pi^*c_2(E)=kH_{\rm top}^2=k\pi^*u$; since $\pi^*u$ is a generator, $c_2(E)=ku$. This is conditional on the pullback hypothesis and asserts no Ward correspondence. [F7, step 5.1, algebra] ∎
